PRD: plans/worktree-lane-lifecycle-prd.md task ω — the B+H integration-gate leaf. Manifest §ω (all PASS; B4 is the load-bearing structural premise). Depends on γ, δ, ε1, ε2. Contract §Boundary-test sketch B1–B6.

WORK — one integration test module orchestrator/tests/test_lane_lifecycle_integration.py driving the GitOps writer ↔ Harness recovery reader ↔ dashboard reader seams both ways (fake/instrumented pool + repo fixture, no real ssh):
- B1 writer→reader round-trip: acquire a lane for task N, run startup recovery → recovery reads .lane-state/<lane>.json, adopts, rebinds N→lane; pool cache matches record.
- B2 crash→quarantine: record ASSIGNED:N but .git/worktrees/<lane> admin entry removed (the 2097/2098 state) → recovery QUARANTINES the lane (moved to quarantine_base + log), does NOT re-pin N; next dispatch clean.
- B3 illegal→escalate: force RELEASED→IN_USE → IllegalLaneTransition raised + a born-at-L2 escalation filed; record unchanged.
- B4 hostile git add -A (CONTAMINATION, load-bearing): agent runs `git add -A && git commit` in a lane whose task wrote plan.json/iterations → the commit stages ZERO .task-meta paths; `git ls-tree` on the commit shows no metadata. (This proves contamination is STRUCTURAL — it must pass with the scrub guards STILL PRESENT here; θ then removes them and re-runs B4.)
- B5 survives cleaning: `git clean -xfd` + `git checkout -f` in a lane → .lane-state record and .task-meta artifacts both intact + readable.
- B6 dashboard reader: dashboard read_task_artifacts over a relocated lane returns plan/phase/iteration data from .task-meta (new-then-old).

User-observable signal: pytest orchestrator/tests/test_lane_lifecycle_integration.py green (B1–B6).
Consumer: task θ (guard deletion is gated on B4 proving contamination structural).
